tasks.title: Preserve the event payload
tasks.contract: Split a string at its first "::". Return {topic,payload}. Preserve every later delimiter in payload. Without a delimiter, payload is empty. Empty topics/payloads are allowed.

tasks.title: Do not turn a rejected job into success
tasks.contract: Given JSON job outcomes {status:"fulfilled",value} or {status:"rejected",reason}, settle the corresponding promises. Return {successes, failures}; values retain input order within each group. Rejection reasons may be null, false, zero or empty strings.

tasks.title: Detect dependency loops without rejecting reuse
tasks.contract: Given an adjacency object whose keys are node names and values are dependency arrays, return true iff any directed cycle exists. A dependency referenced without its own key is a leaf. Reusing a dependency in a DAG is allowed.

tasks.title: Read the value without losing its separator
tasks.contract: Split a manifest line at the first "=" into {key,value}. Preserve later equals signs and all whitespace literally. Lines without "=" have an empty value.

tasks.title: Keep falsy failures in the rejection ledger
tasks.contract: Given JSON operations {reject:boolean,payload}, execute resolve/reject promises accordingly. Return one record per operation: {state:"ok",value} or {state:"failed",reason}. Preserve falsy payloads and original order.

tasks.title: Distinguish route convergence from a loop
tasks.contract: Given edges as [from,to] string pairs, return true iff they contain a directed cycle. Multiple routes can converge on the same destination. An empty edge list has no cycle.

tasks.title: Allow adjacent bookings
tasks.contract: A booking and a slot are half-open integer intervals [start,end), with start <= end. Return true iff their intersection has positive duration. Empty and merely adjacent intervals do not overlap.

tasks.title: Do not restart on an unknown cursor
tasks.contract: Given unique-string IDs, a cursor string or null, and a nonnegative integer limit, return up to limit IDs strictly after the cursor. Null means start. Unknown non-null cursors return an empty list.
